A.explanation: Correct. With $I = 1.0 \text{ A}$ the full $3.0 \, \Omega$ potentiometer drops $3.0 \text{ V}$, which is the largest voltage the slider can tap.

B.explanation: Incorrect. $3.4 \text{ V}$ is close to the p.d. across the $3.0 \, \Omega$ if internal resistance were ignored, but the $1.0 \, \Omega$ reduces the current.

C.explanation: Incorrect. $4.5 \text{ V}$ is half the e.m.f. and ignores that the $5.0 \, \Omega$ and $1.0 \, \Omega$ take most of the $9.0 \text{ V}$.

D.explanation: Incorrect. $5.4 \text{ V}$ is the p.d. across the $5.0 \, \Omega$ plus part of the potentiometer, not the voltage tapped by the voltmeter.

hints: Notice the voltmeter connects the junction of the $5.0 \, \Omega$ resistor and the potentiometer to the sliding contact, so it measures only the p.d. across the left part of the $3.0 \, \Omega$ track.
Recall the whole $1.0 \, \Omega + 5.0 \, \Omega + 3.0 \, \Omega$ loop is in series, so find the current from $I = E / R_{total}$ with $E = 9.0 \text{ V}$.
Connect maximum voltmeter reading to maximum tapped resistance, then use $V = IR$ for that part of the potentiometer.
walkthrough: Identify the circuit: the $1.0 \, \Omega$ internal resistance, $5.0 \, \Omega$ fixed resistor and full $3.0 \, \Omega$ potentiometer are in series.
Total resistance is $R_{total} = 1.0 + 5.0 + 3.0 = 9.0 \, \Omega$, so the loop current is $I = E/R_{total} = 9.0/9.0 = 1.0 \text{ A}$.
The voltmeter reads $V = I \times R_{tapped}$, where $R_{tapped}$ is the resistance between the left end of the potentiometer and the slider.
$R_{tapped}$ is largest when the slider is moved to the far right end, giving $R_{tapped} = 3.0 \, \Omega$.
Hence $V_{max} = 1.0 \times 3.0 = 3.0 \text{ V}$. This is option A.
